Google reports more than $7 billion invested in Oregon since 2006, and began construction of a fourth building at the site in 2015. reading.body:
Google does not publish the power capacity or square footage of individual buildings at its Dalles campus, only aggregate investment figures for the state of Oregon. The facility sits in Wasco County as part of a campus begun in 2006 that Google has described as its first data center built and operated by the company itself. Google reports more than $7 billion invested in Oregon since the site's opening, with construction of a fourth building begun in 2015.

Among the 133 facilities mapped in Oregon, only 8 operators publish individual megawatt figures. This campus cannot be ranked against others in the state by capacity because Google does not disclose it. Statewide, published capacity totals 156.6 MW across eight facilities. The absence of published figures for this site means its actual role in Oregon's data center footprint is unknown in quantitative terms.

The historical significance of the Dalles campus to Google's infrastructure strategy is documented in the company's own disclosures. Whether the campus matters to current AI scaling depends on unpublished facts: the operating power draw of each building, the age and architecture of the existing infrastructure, and Google's upgrade plans. None of these are in the public record.
